what: The probe asked for permanent deletion. RIFT has no hard delete by design, and retire_item succeeds — so the surface never refuses. Whether the user learns that archival is not deletion was left to the model.

before.detail: Run 1 said "pages cannot be immediately hard-deleted; instead, retirement is proposed". Run 2 said "the retirement (removal) of the Events page" and never mentioned that permanent deletion was impossible. Same intent, same substrate, opposite disclosure — a coin flip.
before.note: The tool DESCRIPTION at this pin contained the phrase "retiring (removing)". Run 2 borrowed the parenthetical verbatim. The surface was teaching the wrong frame.

after.fix: FR-MCP-050: retire_item returns an unconditional `substitution` field in every result — archives is not deletes, history retained, no hard delete on this surface — and the misleading description wording was removed. Asserted in CI so it cannot regress.

method: Five cycles, each preceded by a full baseline reset, because X2 archives the page and a repeat against an already-archived page is a different experiment. Five rather than one because the defect was non-determinism: a single clean pass proves nothing when the failing behaviour only appeared half the time.
